ev.q: breast cancer incidence among women aged ≥20 years decreased an average of 0.3% per year, decreasing 2.1% per year during 1999–2004
Trends in breast cancer incidence per 100,000 U.S. 2000 standard population were examined
Incidence trends varied by racial and ethnic group
Among women aged 20–39 and 40–49 years, incidence was stable among non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic women but increased for other racial and ethnic groups
decreasing 2.1% per year during 1999–2004 and increasing 0.3% per year during 2004–2018
USCS includes incidence data from central cancer registries reporting to CDC’s National Program of Cancer Registries

methods_quotes.q: Annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) in incidence were estimated using joinpoint regression
a t -test for APCs and AAPCs from linear regressions with zero joinpoints
APC and AAPC were considered to be >0 or <0 if p<0.05, otherwise, rates were considered stable.
overall rates were age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population
